translationRepairs: Zhuangzong and Liu Xun were locked at Xin. He called Cunju to join forces and strike Xun.
Zhuangzong and Liu Xun were locked at Shen. He called Cunju to join forces and strike Xun.
The standoff is at 莘, which must be distinguished from 新州 already rendered Xin in the preceding sentence.
He was moved to the Transoceanic circuit.
He was moved to the Henghai circuit.
橫海 is the Henghai command; Transoceanic is a false calque.

Hanrong taught Jinquan to detain him and refuse the summons. Client Pang Lingtu urged: “Renzhao once served Wang Yanqiu. When Yanqiu besieged Wang Du at Zhongshan, Du put a crack bowman on the wall who struck Yanqiu’s helmet tassel. Renzhao drew from behind, one arrow, and the bowman fell. Yanqiu hunted for the man to reward him; Renzhao stayed silent—that is loyalty under heaven.

Hanrong taught Jinquan to detain him and refuse the summons. Client Pang Lingtu urged: “Renzhao once served Wang Yanqiu. When Yanqiu besieged Wang Du at Zhongshan, Du put a crack bowman on the wall who struck Yanqiu’s helmet. Renzhao drew from behind, one arrow, and the bowman fell. Yanqiu hunted for the man to reward him; Renzhao stayed silent—that is loyalty under heaven.
中兜牟 means the arrow struck the helmet; the English tassel is not in the Chinese.
Jinquan was raised in Mingzong’s household as a boy. Bold in the saddle and with the bow, he rode on Mingzong’s campaigns and rose to prefect by merit.
In youth Jinquan was a servant in Mingzong’s household. Bold in the saddle and with the bow, he rode on Mingzong’s campaigns and rose to prefect by merit.
廝養 marks menial household service in youth, not merely being reared in the household.
He sent Li Chengyu into An. Jinquan fled south. At Mishui he craned his neck northward, wept, and went on.
He sent Li Chengyu into Anzhou. Jinquan fled south. At Michuan he craned his neck northward, wept, and went on.
入安州 is Anzhou, and 泌川 is Michuan, not Mishui.
Under Han’s Emperor Yin, Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and begged troops of Li Bian. Jinquan, as Li Bian’s Runzhou commissioner, marched with Zha Wenhui and others out of Shuyang.
Under Han’s Emperor Yin, Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and begged troops. Jinquan, as military commissioner of Runzhou, marched with Zha Wenhui and others out of Shuyang.
Li Bian and the possessive on Runzhou are interpolations, but 乞兵於 is a lacuna and must not be filled with “the southern court.”
When the deposed emperor took the throne, Siquan was made Jingnan commissioner.
When the deposed emperor took the throne, Siquan was made military commissioner of the Jingnan Army.
靜難軍節度使 is the Jingnan Army commission promised as Binning, not the Jingnan 荊南 polity.

Bow-and-arrow depot commissioner Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin came forward and said to Gaozu: “Your Lordship is Mingzong’s beloved son and his beloved son-in-law. At such a time you cannot repay the state yet ask where the ministers and the state treasures are—do you aid the rebels?”

Bow-and-arrow depot commissioner Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin came forward and said to Gaozu: “The sovereign is Mingzong’s beloved son; you, sir, are his beloved son-in-law. At such a time you cannot repay the state yet ask where the ministers and the state treasures are—do you aid the rebels?”
主上 is Mingzong’s beloved son (the sovereign); 公 is the son-in-law addressed, not one fused Lordship.

Bow-and-arrow depot commissioner Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin advanced and said to Gaozu: “Your Lordship is Emperor Mingzong’s beloved son, and you his beloved son-in-law—at such a time you cannot repay the state but instead ask where the ministers and state treasures are; do you too aid the rebels?”

Bow-and-arrow depot commissioner Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin advanced and said to Gaozu: “The sovereign is Emperor Mingzong’s beloved son, and you his beloved son-in-law—at such a time you cannot repay the state but instead ask where the ministers and state treasures are; do you too aid the rebels?”
The literal likewise conflates 主上 and 公; they are Emperor Min and Shi Jingtang.
Hongzhi later served Jin as Fengxiang campaign marshal, retired as Minister of the Imperial Clan, died, and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
Hongzhi later served Jin as Fengxiang campaign marshal, retired as Chamberlain for Ceremonials, died, and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
光祿卿 is Chamberlain for Ceremonials, not 宗正卿 Minister of the Imperial Clan.
Hongzhi later served Jin as Fengxiang campaign marshal, retired as Minister of the Imperial Clan, died, and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
Hongzhi later served Jin as Fengxiang campaign marshal, retired as Chamberlain for Ceremonials, died, and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
The same 光祿卿 error is in the literal English.
In youth he knew books somewhat and was skilled at clerkly work. He was Tang’s Xing prefect and made up as a Fanyang yamen officer.
In youth he knew books somewhat and was skilled at clerkly work. He was magistrate of Tangxing and was appointed a Fanyang yamen officer.
唐興令 is the county magistrate of Tangxing; 補范陽牙校 is appointment, not “made up as.”
In youth he knew books somewhat and was skilled at clerkly affairs; he was Tang’s Xing prefect and made up as a Fanyang yamen officer.
In youth he knew books somewhat and was skilled at clerkly affairs; he was magistrate of Tangxing and was appointed a Fanyang yamen officer.
The literal repeats the 唐興令 and 補 errors.
The princess dowager said he was right.”
The Grand Consort’s words are right.”
Shenjiao is still speaking: 太妃語是 affirms the consort’s counsel, reversing speaker and patient in the original.
The princess dowager said he was right.”
The Grand Consort’s words are right.”
The literal reverses the same 太妃語是 attribution.
The Khitan made Zhou Wusheng military commissioner.
The Khitan made Zhou military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.
以周為武勝軍節度使 appoints Zhou to the Wusheng Army; Wusheng is not part of his name.
The note is （行珪附）; the stray 〉 is not in the Chinese, and 行珪 is Xinggui.
The literal has the same stray bracket and spaced Xing Gui.

Li Keyong stationed Liu Rengong at Youzhou, made his elder brother Mo vanguard commander-in-chief, Siji central army commander-in-chief, and a younger brother Mo rear army commander-in-chief—the Gao brothers divided Yan troops among themselves.

Li Keyong stationed Liu Rengong at Youzhou, made his elder brother So-and-so vanguard commander-in-chief, Siji central army commander-in-chief, and a younger brother So-and-so rear army commander-in-chief—the Gao brothers divided Yan troops among themselves.
兄某 and 弟某 are unnamed placeholders; Mo is an invented personal name.
Rengong made his elder brother’s son Xinggui a yamen officer. Xingzhou was barely over ten; he also took him into his tent; as he grew he was given military posts.
Rengong made Siji’s elder brother’s son Xinggui a yamen officer. Xingzhou, Siji’s son, was barely over ten; he also took him into his tent; as he grew he was given military posts.
其兄某之子行珪 is Siji’s unnamed elder brother’s son, and 思繼子行周 is Xingzhou; neither is Rengong’s kin.
Rengong made his elder brother Mo’s son Xinggui a yamen officer, and Xingzhou was barely over ten; he also took him into his tent; as he grew he was given military posts.
Rengong made Siji’s elder brother So-and-so’s son Xinggui a yamen officer, and Siji’s son Xingzhou was barely over ten; he also took him into his tent; as he grew he was given military posts.
某 is not Mo and 其兄某 is Siji’s brother, but the replacement still omits 思繼子 before Xingzhou.

Shouguang was about to have Yuan Xingqin herd horses beyond the mountains. Hearing Shouguang was nearly besieged, he at once led the herd to rescue; but his troops mutinied on the road and installed Xingqin as Youzhou regent. Xingqin said: “What I fear is Xinggui alone.”

Shouguang’s general Yuan Xingqin was herding horses beyond the mountains. Hearing Shouguang was nearly besieged, he at once led the herd to the rescue; but his troops mutinied on the road and installed Xingqin as Youzhou regent. Xingqin said: “What I fear is Xinggui alone.”
守光將元行欽 is Shouguang’s general already herding horses north of the mountains, not a planned future posting.

Shouguang was about to have Yuan Xingqin herd horses beyond the mountains; hearing Shouguang was nearly besieged he at once led the herd to rescue; but his troops mutinied on the road, installed Xingqin as Youzhou regent. Xingqin said: “What I fear is Xinggui alone.”

Shouguang’s general Yuan Xingqin was herding horses beyond the mountains; hearing Shouguang was nearly besieged he at once led the herd to the rescue; but his troops mutinied on the road and installed Xingqin as Youzhou regent. Xingqin said: “What I fear is Xinggui alone.”
The literal repeats the auxiliary misreading of 將.
When Mingzong took the throne he was moved to Wusheng and Anyuan.
When Mingzong took the throne he was moved to Weisheng and Anyuan.
徙鎮威勝 is Weisheng, a different command from 武勝 (Wusheng).
When Mingzong took the throne he was moved to Wusheng and Anyuan.
When Mingzong took the throne he was moved to Weisheng and Anyuan.
The literal likewise collapses 威勝 into Wusheng.

Liang and Jin faced each other on the Yellow River. Zhuangzong sent Mingzong east to strike Yanzhou. Xingzhou led the vanguard. That night it rained; the army all wanted to halt. Xingzhou said: “Heaven is aiding me!

Liang and Jin faced each other on the Yellow River. Zhuangzong sent Mingzong east to strike Yunzhou. Xingzhou led the vanguard. That night it rained; the army all wanted to halt. Xingzhou said: “Heaven is aiding me!
東襲鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou 兗州.

Yan men rely on rain and will not guard against us—strike when they do not expect it."
Yun men rely on rain and will not guard against us—strike when they do not expect it."
鄆人 are the people of Yunzhou, not Yan.
Yan men rely on rain and will not guard against us—strike when they do not expect it."
Yun men rely on rain and will not guard against us—strike when they do not expect it."
The literal likewise renders 鄆人 as Yan.
That night he galloped across the ford into the city. The Yan men only then realized it—and Yanzhou was taken.
That night he galloped across the ford into the city. The Yun men only then realized it—and Yunzhou was taken.
鄆人 and the city taken are Yunzhou, not Yanzhou.
That night he galloped across the ford into the city; the Yan men only then realized it and Yanzhou was taken.
That night he galloped across the ford into the city; the Yun men only then realized it and Yunzhou was taken.
The literal repeats Yan/Yanzhou for 鄆.
He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works and Prince of Qin.
He died and was posthumously made Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Prince of Qin.
贈尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works.
He died; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Qin.
He died; he was posthumously made Director of the Imperial Secretariat and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Qin.
The literal has the same 尚書令 error.
Li Yun, He Ning, and other court men were still at Zhen with the Khitan. Zairong surrounded their houses with troops and extorted goods; he even meant to kill Yun for his property.
Li Song, He Ning, and other court men were still at Zhen with the Khitan. Zairong surrounded their houses with troops and extorted goods; he even meant to kill Song for his property.
李崧 and 崧 are Li Song, not Yun.
At that time Li Yun, He Ning, and others had all stayed at Zhen with the Khitan; Zairong ringed their houses with troops and pressed them for goods, and even wished to kill Yun and take his wealth.
At that time Li Song, He Ning, and others had all stayed at Zhen with the Khitan; Zairong ringed their houses with troops and pressed them for goods, and even wished to kill Song and take his wealth.
The literal repeats Yun for 李崧.
